повезти.gloss: to be lucky (impersonal); to take (by vehicle)

meanings.en: to be lucky (impersonal); to take (by vehicle)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'везти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be lucky', forming an aspectual pair with 'везти'.

examples.trans: You and I got lucky.

examples.text: Повезло тебе, что меня на кастинг пригласили.
examples.trans: You are lucky they invited me to the casting anyway.
I was lucky!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Вика! Ты вообще меня не слушаешь?
examples.trans: Wait, are you not listening to me at all?

examples.text: Или я для тебя пустое место?
examples.trans: Or am I invisible to you?
Vika, did you want to say something?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Am I talking to a wall?
What? Excuse me.
Vitya, what is going on here, pal?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: I still work as a cook.
I finally proposed to Vika.

examples.text: Вика! Ты вообще меня не слушаешь?
examples.trans: Wait, are you not listening to me at all?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Тебе это на канал не пропустят.
examples.trans: They will not let that on television.
For a couple of days.
Set a reminder on your phone.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'casting', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Повезло тебе, что меня на кастинг пригласили.
examples.trans: You are lucky they invited me to the casting anyway.

examples.text: Буду ходить по кастингам и стану актрисой.
examples.trans: I'll go to auditions and become an actress.

examples.text: Я буду работать официанткой. Буду ходить по кастингам и стану актрисой.
examples.trans: I will work as a waitress. I'll go to auditions and become an actress.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'гласить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to invite', forming an aspectual pair with 'приглашать'.

examples.text: Повезло тебе, что меня на кастинг пригласили.
examples.trans: You are lucky they invited me to the casting anyway.

examples.text: Я так и знал, что пригласят.
examples.trans: I knew all along they would invite you.
Call your witness.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have to feed him so well.
Oh, just family stuff.

examples.text: Вы уж извините, что так вышло.
examples.trans: Please forgive me that it turned out this way.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы вернулись в Россию и поженились.
examples.trans: We returned to Russia and got married.

examples.text: Мой карьерный рост был долгим и трудным.
examples.trans: My career climb was long and difficult.

examples.text: Я готовил для президентов России и Франции.
examples.trans: I cooked for the presidents of Russia and France.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Знаете, боюсь, мне это не грозит.
examples.trans: You know, I am afraid that is not a threat for me.
I don't know.
Well, I don't know, Max.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: All right, where is the chef?
Chef, your program is starting on TV.
Cleverly thought out, boss!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'there'.

examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich has just arrived.
Chef, your program is starting on TV.
Everything's fine there.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'cinema', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Chef, your program is starting on TV.
Then invite me to the movies.
So, let's look at the schedule in the cinema.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: How are things with you?
Chef, your program is starting on TV.
Who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (root 'чинаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to begin', forming an aspectual pair with 'начаться'.

examples.trans: Chef, your program is starting on TV.
War begins again!

examples.text: Спасибо, теперь для нас начинается новая жизнь.
examples.trans: Thank you, now a new life begins for us.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, go ahead and turn it on.
All right, here you go.
OK, I'm coming.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('let's') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Let's clean up!
See you, bye!
Arkasha, let's clean up!

включать.gloss: to turn on, to plug in

meanings.en: to turn on, to plug in
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to turn on', forming an aspectual pair with 'включить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: All right, go ahead and turn it on.
Ninul, plug in the soldering iron.

examples.text: Он всегда включает свет на кухне.
examples.trans: He always switches on the kitchen light.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('we') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: We recently returned from Paris.

examples.text: Мы вернулись в Россию и поженились.
examples.trans: We returned to Russia and got married.
We have an ideal family.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'by chance'.

examples.text: Мы случайно обнаружили ещё одну запись.
examples.trans: We accidentally found one more recording.
Are you by any chance Samson?
I met him by chance.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (root 'наружить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to discover', forming an aspectual pair with 'обнаруживать'.

examples.text: Мы случайно обнаружили ещё одну запись.
examples.trans: We accidentally found one more recording.
The doctors discovered an aneurysm in the patient.
The experts detected a hidden mistake.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.

examples.trans: Who else would fry pancakes like these?

examples.text: Ещё утром. А что это меняет?
examples.trans: Back this morning. What does that change?

examples.text: Мы случайно обнаружили ещё одну запись.
examples.trans: We accidentally found one more recording.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian num meaning 'one', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
I have one brother.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'recording', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Мы случайно обнаружили ещё одну запись.
examples.trans: We accidentally found one more recording.
Is it recording?
I listened to the recording of the conversation.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to decide', forming an aspectual pair with 'решать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: We decided to show it.
The court has decided.
I've decided.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Find some mistake of hers.

examples.text: Тогда она не сможет тебя упрекнуть.
examples.trans: Then she won't be able to reproach you.
She is also a very famous chef.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'казать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to show', forming an aspectual pair with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: We decided to show it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (root 'волить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Я тебя уволил! Открой дверь, я считаю до трёх.
examples.trans: You are fired! Open the door, I am counting to three.

examples.text: А вы не боитесь, что он вас уволит?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to cook', forming an aspectual pair with 'приготовить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: You need to act more natural, understand?
